newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks tumble, spooked by barred broker Delta.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks tumble, spooked by barred broker Delta.

text.p: Greek shares lost composure on Thursday plunging 2.26 percent to a session low of 911.14 on the benchmark index before trimming losses to close 1.52 percent lower in moderate trading volume of 5.4 billion drachmas.

The market opened weak and brokers said players were spooked by rumours on broker Delta Securities which was barred from trading again on Thursday for non-compliance with settlement regulations with the clearing house.

"There is no question it affected market sentiment. There are rumours Delta is in the red for 1.5 billion drachmas and many are concerned over a possible chain reaction. It seems that finally bourse authorities are clamping down on short-sellers. The knife has hit the bone," said a floor trader who wanted to remain anonymous.
Delta Securities had encountered problems with bourse authorities on Tuesday and had its trading terminals on the floor of the exchange shut down for failing to meet settlement regulations.

Its officers were unavailable for comment and no one was picking up the phones at its offices on Thursday. Two more brokers were suspended from trade on Wednesday for the same reason -- Portalakis and Katsoulis Securities.

"It's hard to say how stocks will react in the next two days, we may have seen a bottom today but there is no doubt the market was spooked by the development with Delta," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.
The Athens general share index closed down 1.52 percent or 14.15 points lower at 918.13 with losers outpacing gainers 174 to 34 with 26 stocks unchanged.
